description:
Napoleon Hill said if the devil can’t destroy you, he’ll distract you.

Not with something obviously bad.

With something almost good.

Another opportunity.
Another idea.
Another notification.
Another reason to delay the work that actually matters.

Most people don’t fail because they’re incapable.

They fail because they lose focus.

Every day you’re either moving closer to the person you’re meant to become or you’re being pulled away from it by a thousand tiny distractions.

The danger isn’t that you’ll choose the wrong path.

The danger is that you’ll never stay on one long enough to see where it leads.

Protect your attention.

Your future is hiding behind the things you’ve been putting off.
transcript: According to Napoleon Hill, the devil's greatest tool is distraction. If the devil can't destroy you, let's think of that inner villain, that other voice. If it can't destroy you directly, then the second option is distraction. Gets you busy doing busy things. Gets you busy doing things that don't move the needle.
